In addition, the mosque is made by Ottoman-designed. The roof, a narthex, and porticos are covering the main prayer hall. From the porticos, rise two minarets to the height of 28 meters.The minarets are octagonal and adorned with conical tops and finials. The lead and glass are decorating the minarets with imitation stones. The walls of the Mosque contain murals; depicting Quranic inscriptions and Islamic symbology. The calligraphic adeptness of these murals is phenomenal and bears a proud testimony to the skills of Persian artists. Guangdong Province has long been one of China's pioneers in opening up. As the country's leading provincial trader, Guangdong is deepening economic ties with the Asia-Pacific through trade, innovation and closer cooperation. From coffee machines made in Shunde to robots developed through Guangdong-Hong Kong collaboration, companies are finding new opportunities across the region.
The province has been China's largest provincial trader for 40 years, with last year's imports and exports topping 9 trillion yuan (about 1.3 trillion US dollars) and more than 20 million market entities. Shunde is now the world's largest coffee machine production base, with Gemilai alone shipping to over 60 countries and selling more than two million units. Leveraging the Greater Bay Area's innovation hub, Guangdong is also advancing Guangdong-Hong Kong robotics projects and, as Shenzhen hosts APEC this year, aims to deepen regional industrial and supply-chain links for shared growth.

1128019087843725077.desc: As China hosts APEC 2026, regional integration is taking center stage. In southern China's Greater Bay Area, cities like Zhuhai, Hengqin, and Macao are operating like a single supply chain network, linking automated factories with global talent and capital. To see how this cross-border teamwork helps brands go global, CGTN's Yu Hongyu takes us inside a hair dryer factory in Zhuhai.

1128019087843725079.desc: Carbon fiber-once reserved for aerospace and elite racing-is now powering a much broader industrial shift across the Asia-Pacific. CGTN's Yu Hongyu explores how this featherlight thread is is driving billions in APEC trade.

1128019087843725080.desc: You flip a switch, and the lights come on. But where does that power come from? In Yangjiang, Guangdong, the answer lies offshore.
